chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Salih, from one of the elders of the Banu al-Najashiyy, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The head (chief) of obedience to Allah is patience and satisfaction with Allah regarding what the servant loves or dislikes; and a servant will not be satisfied with Allah regarding what he loves or dislikes, except that it is better for him regarding what He loves or dislikes.
ai.seo_question: What is the highest form of obedience to Allah according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In Shia theology, this hadith elevates *al-Rida* (contentment) from mere passive endurance to an active, conscious acceptance of Divine Will, serving as the spiritual foundation for *Sabr*. It underscores the principle that true obedience requires aligning one's heart with Allah's wisdom, ensuring that both blessings and trials yield benefit for the believer. This concept is central to the journey of the soul (*suluk*) in achieving closeness to the Divine through unwavering trust.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu UUmeyr, from Jameel Bin Salih, from one of the Sheykhs of the clan of Al Najjashy, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The chief of obedience to Allah<sup>azwj</sup> is the patience and the satisfaction from Allah<sup>azwj</sup> regarding whatever the servant loves or abhors; and a servant would not be satisfied from Allah<sup>azwj</sup> regarding whatever he loves or abhors except it was better for him regarding what He<sup>azwj</sup> Loves or Abhors’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Jamil ibn Salih from certain shaykhs of Banu al-Najashi from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “

The head of obedience to Allah is patience and agreeing with the decisions of Allah in all matters whether a servant may love or dislike doing so. Of the servant of Allah anyone who agrees with the decisions of Allah in all matters which he loves or dislikes, should know that agreeing, in fact, is in his best interest.”
